overview: Two essential tools of genetic engineering with opposite jobs — one cuts DNA, the other joins it.
genZNote: Restriction enzyme: molecular scissors. DNA ligase: molecular glue stick.

aspects.label: Action on DNA
aspects.valueA: Cuts DNA at specific recognition sequences (restriction sites).
aspects.valueB: Joins DNA fragments together by forming phosphodiester bonds.

aspects.label: Role in Gene Cloning
aspects.valueA: Cuts both the gene of interest and the vector to create compatible sticky/blunt ends.
aspects.valueB: Seals the gene of interest into the cut vector, forming recombinant DNA.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueB: T4 DNA ligase (commonly used in labs).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: EcoRI recognises the palindromic sequence GAATTC and cuts to leave sticky ends — a classic named-enzyme NEET fact.
overlay.commonMisconception: Restriction enzymes don't cut DNA randomly — they recognise very specific palindromic sequences.
